items.followUp: What are the two products of alcoholic fermentation?

rubric.why: The definition identifies fermentation as the breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
rubric.description: Defines fermentation as the anaerobic breakdown of glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down in the absence of oxygen; accept an equivalent definition that also mentions incomplete breakdown or release of energy.

rubric.why: These are the two main types of fermentation.
rubric.description: Names both types of fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark only when both alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation are named.

modelAnswer: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose, releasing a small amount of energy.
Its two types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

items.followUp: Where do the dark reactions of photosynthesis take place?

rubric.why: The key feature of dark reactions is that they do not directly depend on light.
rubric.description: Explains that dark reactions do not require light directly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reactions are light-independent or do not require light directly.

rubric.why: Dark reactions use products of the light reactions to fix carbon dioxide into carbohydrates.
rubric.description: States that carbon dioxide is used to form carbohydrates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the use of carbon dioxide to make carbohydrates; mention of the stroma or ATP and NADPH may support the answer.

modelAnswer: Dark reactions are the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis; they do not require light directly.
They use carbon dioxide and products of the light reactions to form carbohydrates in the chloroplast stroma.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme-substrate complex, and how does it help an enzyme speed up a reaction?

rubric.why: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed to initiate a chemical reaction.
rubric.description: Defines activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the minimum energy required to start or initiate a reaction.

rubric.why: Enzymes speed reactions by providing a pathway with a lower activation-energy requirement.
rubric.description: Explains how enzymes lower activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that enzymes provide an alternative pathway or form an enzyme-substrate complex that lowers the energy barrier.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum energy required to initiate a chemical reaction.
An enzyme lowers it by providing an alternative reaction pathway, often through formation of an enzyme-substrate complex.

items.followUp: Give one example of an extracellular enzyme and state where it acts.

rubric.why: Intracellular enzymes carry out their reactions inside cells.
rubric.description: Distinguishes intracellular enzymes by their site of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that intracellular enzymes act inside the cell.

rubric.why: Extracellular enzymes are released from cells and act outside them.
rubric.description: Distinguishes extracellular enzymes by their site of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that extracellular enzymes are secreted and act outside the cell.

modelAnswer: Intracellular enzymes remain and act inside the cell, for example enzymes involved in cellular respiration.
Extracellular enzymes are secreted by cells and act outside the cell, for example digestive enzymes acting in the gut.

items.followUp: What is a coenzyme? Give one example.

rubric.why: A cofactor is a non-protein component needed for enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Defines cofactors as non-protein components required by enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cofactors are non-protein substances required for an enzyme to function.

rubric.why: Cofactors may be metal ions, coenzymes or prosthetic groups.
rubric.description: Names a type of cofactor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving at least one correct type or example of a cofactor.

modelAnswer: Cofactors are non-protein substances required by some enzymes for their activity.
They include metal ions, coenzymes and prosthetic groups.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a population and an ecosystem.

rubric.why: A population consists of members of one species living in a defined area.
rubric.description: Describes population level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying individuals of the same species and 1 mark for specifying that they live in the same area or at the same time.

rubric.why: A community is made up of populations of different species living and interacting in one area.
rubric.description: Describes community level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying populations of different species and 1 mark for stating that they live or interact in the same area.

modelAnswer: Population level: A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
Members of a population can interact and reproduce with one another.
Community level: A community consists of the populations of different species living in the same area.
The organisms in a community interact with one another.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of a chloroplast and explain its role in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.description: States the general features of plastids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plastids as organelles in plant cells and noting their double membrane.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Describes chloroplasts and their function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chlorophyll-containing chloroplasts with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.description: Describes chromoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain coloured pigments or give colour to plant parts.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.description: Describes leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that leucoplasts are colourless or store food.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts can store substances such as starch, oils and proteins.
rubric.description: Gives examples of stored materials or the major types of plastids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming stored materials or describing amyloplasts, elaioplasts or proteinoplasts.

modelAnswer: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis; their internal membranes form thylakoids arranged in grana within the stroma.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments that give colour to flowers and fruits.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
Leucoplasts may store starch, oils or proteins.

items.followUp: Explain two ways biodiversity supports the stability of ecosystems.

rubric.why: Biodiversity provides people with useful biological resources.
rubric.description: Explains biodiversity as a source of useful products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming two useful resources such as food, medicines, fuel, clothing or raw materials.

rubric.why: Species contribute to ecosystem processes that support life and agriculture.
rubric.description: Describes ecosystem services provided by biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining at least two ecosystem services, such as pollination, nutrient cycling or maintaining soil fertility.

rubric.why: Biodiversity helps maintain environmental conditions and resources.
rubric.description: Explains biodiversity's role in maintaining environmental quality.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing benefits such as water purification, protection of water resources or climate regulation.

rubric.why: A variety of species and genetic resources helps ecosystems and agriculture remain resilient.
rubric.description: Explains biodiversity's contribution to resilience or genetic resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking species diversity with ecosystem stability or identifying genetic resources useful in agriculture.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity provides useful resources, including food, medicines, fuel, clothing and raw materials.
Different organisms support ecosystem services such as pollination, nutrient cycling and the maintenance of soil fertility.
Biodiversity helps protect water resources and contributes to water purification and climate stability.
A variety of species and genetic resources helps maintain stable ecosystems and supports agriculture.
